Revised assessment: The statement remains cautious about near-term activity, employment, and inflation because of the pandemic, but it also commits to powerful support—zero policy rates, ongoing Treasury and MBS purchases, and average-inflation targeting aimed at a temporary overshoot. In Taylor-rule–consistent New Keynesian frameworks (e.g., Clarida–Galí–Gertler), such forward guidance and commitment to overshooting lower real rates and help anchor expectations; evidence on QE transmission via the term structure (Cochrane–Piazzesi) and the credit channel (Bernanke–Gertler) indicates these purchases can ease longer-term borrowing costs and sustain the flow of credit. Net tone: cautious on the outlook but clearly dovish on policy, yielding a mildly negative overall sentiment rather than strongly negative.
